Question: Is it possible that Jesus Christ was a mutant with defying powers like resurrection, as suggested by Exodus in Marvel's Immortal X-Men?
Answer: The thing about Exodus is that he is a religious fanatic. A Christian religious fanatic. This is not figurative. Exodus literally believes the cross is inscribed on the genes of every mutant. He perceives the world in terms of prophecy and messiahs. Dragons and revelation. According to Hope Summers his own powers are partially powered by faith. He was a crusader who was abducted by Apocalypse and transformed. Exodus rejected Apocalypse because he considered him the devil. Exodus is extremely powerful, an Omega-level telekinetic. But he is also gripped with a religious mania that is endlessly seeking the true messiah. Is it possible that, within the Marvel universe, the historical Jesus was a mutant with resurrection powers? Yes, that is possible. That would not even be close to the strangest thing that Marvel has done. But, far more likely, Exodus is simply filled with religious conviction that does not match reality. In Marvel we know, for certain, that Heaven exists. It is a place that Reed Richards once built a machine to get him to. We know God exists. We know Angels exist (and not just the Angels that Angela belongs to). In Marvel, Christian theology is probably exactly what it appears to be, and Exodus just believes a strange and personal heresy. Religious fervor will lead a person to strange places.

Question: Do you think the X-Men's Rogue is stronger than the Hulk in X-Men '97 based on the events of "Bright Eyes"?
Answer: Stronger? Probably not. But here’s the thing, every single time someone comes up with something “strong enough to hold the Hulk” they’re always wrong. The people who Hulk proof things have a truly atrocious track record. They are chronically over confidant. Is Rogue much, much, much stronger than the people tasked with containing the Hulk think she is? Obviously yes. Are they also much less capable of dealing with someone who also has been trained to actually fight as opposed to just smash? Yes. Does her maneuverability, particularly her ability to traverse all three dimensions of a battlefield, give her considerable advantage over everything they have prepared for? Again, yes. I think it would be odd to rank Rogue as stronger than the Hulk. But that doesn't mean she isn't damn strong. And if you are building things to fight the Hulk, she will be more than you can handle. Hulk is strongest there is. Rogue is real freakin’ close ro that.

Question: What impact do you think the shift in focus from established dramas to new and diverse shows will have on the Emmy Awards landscape?
Answer: Of the 75th Primetime Emmy Nominees for Outstanding Drama, only The Crown, Succession, and Better Call Saul had their final seasons. B B, The Last of Us, White Lotus, Andor, and Yellowjackets were all renewed and have seasons upcoming. And yet none of them managed to air in the eligibility window for this year's Emmys. The year before Euphoria, Severance, Squid Game, and Stranger Things all were renewed with upcoming seasons. They all missed not just one, but two Emmy eligibility windows. The 76th Emmys having only one returning drama nominee, The Crown, does not reflect a change in the content of televison or a change in the taste of the Academy. It reflects a structural change in how TV is made. Even as episode counts keep shrinking, production hiatuses keep getting longer. The breaks between seasons keep getting longer and longer. So shows that are Emmy locks keep missing eligibility windows. Instead of, as has been traditional, a fairly stable slate of nominees featuring shows that get nominated year after year, it is an unstable group of nominees which just consists of whoever made a season that year. This is more exciting. And something like Fallout, which would almost certainly get crowded out in previous years, now can scure a nomination. But it also is extremely frustrating because the wait times between seasons are just killing any momentum those shows achieve. I loved Squid Game, but I really am struggling to care about season two because it has just been so long. Same thing with Severence. Some of this is just addiction to celebrity. Casting Pedro Pascal in your zombie show can generate a lot of hype, but filming will have to work around a very busy schedule. Some of this is just structural issues since Covid. A lot of it is just poor management by streaming services. And significantly lower pay given to creative teams, necessitating them not being able to focus on single projects. But the shift from previously established dramas is not because of the Academy becoming disillusioned with those dramas. House of the Dragon is absolutely going to get a nomination next year. It is all about shows missing eligibility windows.
